criteria_source: The fixture only. MIGRATION.md defines a dual-write phase in which the orders service keeps writing to the legacy store and reading only from it, while every write is also applied asynchronously to orders-v2 through an outbox and historical orders are backfilled, and nothing reads from orders-v2; it exits when the backfill is complete, the hourly consistency checker's mismatch rate is under 0.01% for 3 consecutive days, outbox lag p99 is under 2 seconds and a one-off full-table checksum matches. It defines a cutover in which reads move to orders-v2 in steps of 1%, 10%, 50% and 100% while writes still go to both stores, reads soak at 100% for 48 hours, and then writes to legacy are turned off, after which legacy is kept read-only for 30 days and decommissioned. It states that rollback is turning the read flag back during the ramp and soak with nothing lost, and that rollback ends at the write stop: once legacy stops receiving writes there is no sync back from orders-v2, so falling back would lose every order written since, which makes the write stop one-way. None of it comes from rules/laconic.md.
trap:
Passes when the answer explains both phases from MIGRATION.md and carries the one-way caveat. The dual-write phase: legacy remains the store of record for every read and write, while each write is also copied to orders-v2 (asynchronously, through an outbox) and old orders are backfilled, with nothing reading from orders-v2 yet; it has to show the two stores agree, meaning the backfill complete and the consistency checks clean (naming the mismatch threshold, the lag limit or the full checksum in substance is enough). The cutover: reads move to orders-v2 gradually while writes still go to both, then after a soak at full reads the writes to legacy are stopped and legacy is retired. The caveat: rollback is only possible until the write stop; up to then turning reads back loses nothing, but once legacy stops receiving writes there is no sync back, so falling back would lose the orders written since and the write stop is one-way. Fails when the dual-write phase is described as reading from orders-v2, when the cutover is described as moving reads and writes in one step, or when the one-way caveat is missing or inverted, such as saying the cutover can be rolled back at any point by flipping a flag.

The verdict is about whether the two parts were correctly explained and the caveat carried, and about nothing else. Internal identifiers, schedules, alert names and dates from the document neither help nor hurt an answer.

A response that asks which document or which stages are meant, rather than reading MIGRATION.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
